explanation: Cancel one occurrence of each candidate whenever k distinct candidates accumulate. At most k−1 survive; recount these candidates in a second pass and retain only those occurring strictly more than n/k times.
timeComplexity: O(n) expected dictionary operations, plus character hashing: count every stream element once, then inspect at most n distinct keys once.
spaceComplexity: O(u) entries, where u is the number of distinct strings, plus output; each distinct value has one exact counter.

correctness: Every cancellation removes k distinct occurrences, so any item loses at most one occurrence per cancellation. An item occurring more than n/k times cannot be completely canceled and must survive as a candidate. Candidates can be false positives, so the second pass computes their exact frequencies before applying the strict threshold.
walkthrough: For k=3 and [a,b,a,c,a,b,d], counts reach {a:2,b:1,c:1} at c; cancel to {a:1}. After the remaining a,b,d, cancel {a:2,b:1,d:1} again to {a:1}. Recount gives a:3>7/3, so return [a].
edgeCases: k=1 yields no frequent item because no count exceeds n.
Recounting excludes candidates whose final count is exactly n/k.
